subject: Career
title: The First 30 Seconds
description: A micro-lesson that makes The First 30 Seconds usable.

hook.text: Researchers found interviewers often decide in the first 30 seconds. The rest is confirmation.

buildup.text: Your handshake, eye contact, and opening words create an anchor the brain won't easily update.

discovery.text: This is the anchoring effect — first data point shapes all future interpretation.

twist.text: A stumbled greeting can be overcome, but it costs you energy fighting uphill the entire interview.

climax.text: Prepare your first sentence like a speech. Practice it until it's natural.

punchline.text: First impressions aren't fair. But they're real.

quiz.question: What cognitive bias makes the first 30 seconds so critical?

details.summary: Research shows interviewers form a strong initial impression within the first thirty seconds of meeting a candidate. This snap judgment, driven by the primacy effect, disproportionately shapes the entire interview evaluation.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding that first impressions carry outsized weight lets you invest preparation time where it has the highest return: your entrance, handshake, and opening statement.
takeaways: Arrive composed; rushed candidates trigger negative first impressions
A genuine smile activates the interviewer's mirror neurons
Your opening sentence should convey confidence without arrogance

faq.question: Can you recover from a bad first impression in an interview?
faq.answer: It is possible but difficult. The primacy effect means early information anchors all subsequent evaluation. You would need to deliver exceptionally strong answers for the remainder of the interview to overcome the initial negative bias.

faq.question: What specific behaviors create the strongest positive first impression?
faq.answer: A firm handshake, steady eye contact, a warm smile, and a confident greeting that includes the interviewer's name. Standing tall with open body language and speaking at a moderate pace also signal competence and warmth simultaneously.
